messages:
pranav: Heads-up — acme-velocity (acct 4321) just escalated to Hana (CSM). Their P95 for /v1/generate is ~3.6s and we're seeing intermittent 502s since 08:27 PST. They're on a call. Need engineering commit and quick workaround. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-7892

hana-csm: On the call now — customer is concerned about SLA breach window. Asking for ETA on mitigation and whether we can route them to Dedicated or degrade model as temporary measure.

ashley: Oncall +1. I can grab triage; assigning to platform first pass. Is there a specific model or route causing the spike?

mike: Initial look: trend shows increased latency correlated with requests hitting rtx-pool-3 (us-west). KV-cache miss rate up 8x. Some worker restarts around 08:25. Possible memory thrash.

mike: Quick paste of recent logs:
```
[2026-03-17T08:24:58Z] worker-12: kv-cache miss spike (prefix=acme/ctx) -> mem_free 1.2GB
[2026-03-17T08:25:12Z] worker-12: runtime: segfault retry -> reconnect
[2026-03-17T08:25:38Z] proxy: 502 backend error -> downstream
```

liz: If it's pool-specific, immediate mitigations: 1) Move traffic to another pool, 2) Fallback to smaller model variant, or 3) Toggle KV caching strategy for this customer to bypass large prefixes. Which is lowest risk to implement now?

ashley: 1 (move traffic) is highest-confidence; can we route acme-velocity to rtx-pool-1 (same region) for the next 30m? I can update routing policy if someone approves and confirms capacity.

pranav: Please confirm capacity before routing. Customer expects minimal disruption. If we route, preserve pinning and telemetry.

mike: rtx-pool-1 has ~20% headroom right now for their current qps. We can do a manual route for the customer via the console. Plan: migrate 100% of their API key to pool-1, monitor for 10m, if stable keep and then schedule deeper fix.

liz: Ownership: mike to run migration and monitoring. ashley to coordinate rollback plan and comms. pranav to confirm with Hana when we switch. I'll draft a short postmortem checklist if this is persistent.

mike: Executing migration now — command:
```
# route apikey -> pool-1
redwood route update --key acme-4321 --pool rtx-pool-1 --dry-run=false
```

mike: Migration done at 08:35 PST. Initial perf: P95 dropped to 0.9s for the next 2 minutes, no 502s observed. Continuing to monitor.

hana-csm: Reported to customer: "We rolled your traffic to a nearby pool and are monitoring — will confirm in 15 minutes and follow up with a permanent remediation plan." They appreciated the quick action. :thumbsup:

pranav: Good. Next steps: mike to open internal postmortem ticket with logs + root cause hypothesis, liz to propose durable remediation (KV cache limits per-tenant + autoscale), ashley to file an RFC for routing failure modes. Can we get rough ETAs?

mike: Postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-7893 — will have initial writeup by EOD PST.

liz: I'll draft remediation proposal by EOD tomorrow. Includes: per-tenant cache quota, better eviction heuristics, and pool-level soft-limits.

ashley: RFC on routing failure modes targeted next sprint kickoff (2026-03-23). I'll include runbook updates for emergency manual routing.

pranav: For the customer SLA timeline: hana, can you confirm if they consider the incident resolved once P95 < 1s for 30m?

hana-csm: They want a 30m stable window and an internal ticket with a clear fix ETA. Accepts our temporary mitigation for now.

mike: Monitoring note: will keep alerts muted for noise but escalate if p95 exceeds 2s again. Last check (08:44 PST): p95 0.92s, error rate normal.

liz: Thanks team. I'll run a quick dependency check with eng-runtime and infra tomorrow AM (sync invite incoming).

pranav: Closing loop here — thanks everyone for quick responses. We'll reconvene if metrics degrade. :eyes:
